root_cause: The binomial coefficient C(k,p) is computed via successive multiplication followed by division (`c *= (k-p+h); c /= h;`), which can transiently produce a much larger intermediate value than the final coefficient before the division reduces it, allowing the running product to exceed the range representable by int64_t when the bitstream supplies large nb_slots/nb_tr_slots values that lead to numerous large h/k/p iterations. No overflow guard or early termination existed to keep intermediate products bounded.
findings: decode_tsd() incrementally computes the binomial coefficient c = C(k, p) using a multiply-then-divide loop: `c *= k - p + h; c /= h;`.
